# Johnny / Jeremy
Date: 2026-09-21 | Duration: 19m

## Summary
Work priorities included Johnny Martinez owning the feature-flag detail page and coordinating with Gabe on experiments-page designs, while Jeremy Dorn recommended collaboration because the flows are broad and frequently used. The feature-flag design kickoff was deferred until later in the week; Johnny will schedule it after release work, and Jeremy will check availability with Bryce and the team. The release was scheduled for tonight, metrics were near completion, and additional punch-list changes were expected. Data-source onboarding was prioritized because only about 10% of users complete the current flow. The proposed improvements include making the managed warehouse the clear default, positioning own-data connections for advanced users, removing the data-source model and logo-selection steps, simplifying the modal-heavy flow, and supporting partial save and resume. BigQuery OAuth was considered; BigQuery covers 80% of sources, BigQuery and Snowflake about 90%, and Postgres raises coverage to about 95%. Johnny will work on onboarding screens with Jeremy. Homepage direction needs more design work, Johnny will check Nobu’s existing work, and Jeremy will send a design-sync invite for tomorrow.

## Keywords
Feature flags, Data-source onboarding, BigQuery OAuth, Experiment assignment queries, Homepage design, UX prioritisation

# Johnny / Jeremy
Date: 2026-10-13 | Duration: 30m

## Summary
The team considered whether the homepage or settings should be included in the next release, with the homepage closer to release because Nobu had completed related work. Settings scope and ownership remain unclear, particularly around layout, sidebar search, save behavior, and production readiness; delivering both surfaces within two weeks is uncertain. Near-term UI cleanup will align NIAT work with the new settings layout, while Jeremy continues homepage, settings, and related UI work. For feature flags, the preferred approach uses flexible, custom-named environments and must support customers with 50 environments. The interface should represent on/off flags, partial targeting, long values, JSON, rule traffic, fallback behavior, and prerequisite explanations without overwhelming users. Status views should emphasize effective served states and remain mostly read-only, with separate editing flows for publishing and approvals. Detail and list views are especially important for validating AI-created metrics, while the broader product refresh may take a couple months. The team also identified gaps in design-system guidance and agent-generated UI quality.

## Keywords
Feature flags, Prerequisites, Release planning, Settings UI, Design system, AI agents

# Johnny / Jeremy
Date: 2026-10-19 | Duration: 26m

## Summary
The discussion established the UI refresh scope, prioritizing Dashboard, Attributes, and Environments while deferring Save Groups because a new save group type would add complexity. Onboarding should explicitly collect attributes, identifiers, and environments, including environment selection from five options and drag-and-drop ordering. Production environments should be identified separately so stricter controls and approval flows can apply, while QA testing remains enabled outside production. Identifiers will use a separate table and add flow, with no filtering, sorting, or pagination expected. AI dashboard creation was prioritized through a modal offering Start Blank or Start From AI, with users describing the desired dashboard in text. Homepage changes include removing Running Now, keeping Needs Attention prominent, improving dashboard selection, and moving dashboards above the fold. Johnny owns homepage adjustments, while Jeremy will help communicate ownership of resizable attribute-table columns. Initial feedback on the Fact Table direction was positive, pending further alignment.

## Keywords
Dashboard UX, Homepage redesign, Environment configuration, Attribute management, Identifier management, AI dashboard creation
